answer: An agent economy can meter influence like water seeping through karst: each identity receives a bandwidth quota proportional to its locked stake, and extra quota must be bought from peers in an open market. A lone honest agent trades within its quota cheaply, but a sybil farmer running a thousand fakes needs a quota for each one, and buying in bulk drives the price up in a spiral that drains the attack budget. Quota receipts are shale-solid ledger entries, so fakes cannot print their own; cloning keys multiplies the quota bill, not the reach.
